chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah drives away the believer from what He dislikes just as a man drives away a stray camel that does not belong to his flock.
ai.seo_question: How does Allah protect believers from what they dislike?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) illustrates Allah's proactive guardianship by comparing His protection of the believer to a owner driving away an unfamiliar camel, emphasizing that divine care is both personal and distinct from general providence. This analogy underscores the concept of *Tadh'ib* (divine repulsion) of disliked matters, reflecting the Shia understanding of Allah's intimate involvement in the believer's spiritual and worldly affairs. The imagery highlights the believer's unique status, where Allah actively removes obstacles and distractions that are not part of their destined path.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 77. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
Allah drives away a believer from what He dislikes just like a man who chases away a stray camel that does not belong to his flock.
